 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2. Significant Accounting Policies (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">entitled to receive a majority of the VIE&#146;s residual
returns, or both. See note &#147;14. Investments and Variable Interest Entities&#148; for
a discussion of the Company&#146;s variable interest entities.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company formally documents all relationships
between hedging instruments and hedged items, as well as its risk management
objectives and strategies for undertaking the hedge transactions. The Company
utilizes a fixed to floating interest rate swap to hedge the fair value
exposure on its three-, four- and five-year senior notes due 2006, 2007 and
2008 with a face value of $700,000,000. See note &#147;7. Debt.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the interest rate
swap contract, the Company agreed to receive a fixed rate payment for a
floating rate payment. Since the fair value hedge is perfectly effective under
the guidelines of Financial Accounting Standards Board No.&nbsp;133 &#147;Accounting
for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#148;, the changes in the fair
value of the interest rate swap are expected to perfectly offset the changes in
the fair value of the senior notes. On a quarterly basis, the Company adjusts
the carrying amount of the swap to its fair value and adjusts the carrying
amount of the senior notes by the same amount to reflect its change in its fair
value attributable to the hedged risk. There is no hedge ineffectiveness to be
recorded to earnings. The Company monitors the credit ratings of the counter
party and obtains fair value swap valuations from the counter parties and third
parties on a quarterly basis.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Earnings per Share</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is required to
calculate basic earnings per share, which is computed by dividing income
available to common stockholders (the numerator) by the weighted-average number
of common shares outstanding (the denominator) during the period. Income
available to common stockholders is computed by deducting both the dividends
declared in the period on preferred stock (whether or not paid) and dividends
accumulated for the period on cumulative preferred stock (whether or not
earned) from net income. The Company is also required to compute diluted
earnings per share, which is similar to basic earnings per share, except that
the denominator is increased to include the number of additional common shares
that would have been outstanding if the dilutive potential common shares had
been issued.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property and
Equipment and Related Depreciation</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property and equipment,
including capital leases, are carried at historical cost. Depreciation is
provided using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the
assets. The cost of property and equipment and the related accumulated
depreciation are removed from the accounts upon retirement or disposal of such
assets. The resulting gain or loss, if any, is recognized upon the disposition.
Land improvements are depreciated up to 15 years, buildings and improvements
are depreciated up to 40 years, broadcast equipment over 5 to 20 years and
furniture, computer and other equipment over 3 to 7 years. Leasehold
improvements and transponder equipment, which are capitalized, are amortized
over the shorter of their useful life or the remaining life of the lease.
Repairs and maintenance costs are expensed by the Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Significant

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred Financing
Costs</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred financing costs
are amortized over the life of the related debt using the straight-line method,
which is not materially different than the effective interest method.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Program Rights for
Television Broadcast</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Costs incurred in
connection with the production of or purchase of rights to programs to be
broadcast within one year are classified as current assets, while costs of
those programs to be broadcast beyond a one year period are considered
non-current. Program costs are charged to operating expense as the programs are
broadcast. The rights fees related to the 2002/2006 World Cups and other
interim FIFA events are being amortized using the flow of income method.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income Taxes</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses the
liability method of accounting for income taxes. Deferred taxes are provided
for temporary differences between amounts of assets and liabilities for
financial reporting purposes and such amounts as measured by tax laws. See note
&#147;11. Income Taxes.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recent Accounting
Pronouncements</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004, the
FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;153, &#147;Exchange of Nonmonetary Assets,&#148; which is an
amendment of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;29, &#147;Accounting for Nonmonetary
Transactions.&#148; The guidance in APB Opinion No.&nbsp;29 is based on the
principle that exchanges of nonmonetary assets should be measured based on the
fair value of the assets exchanged, with certain exceptions to that principle.
SFAS No.&nbsp;153 eliminates the exception for nonmonetary exchanges of similar
productive assets and replaces it with a general exception for exchanges of
nonmonetary assets that do not have commercial substance. A nonmonetary
exchange has commercial substance if the future cash flows of the entity are
expected to change significantly as a result of the exchange. The Company
adopted SFAS No.&nbsp;153 on its effective date of July&nbsp;1, 2005. The
effect on the Company&#146;s financial position and results of operations will
depend on the significance of television and radio station swap transactions the
Company enters into in the future.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Related
Party Transactions</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Televisa and Venevision,
which are principal stockholders of the Company, have program license
agreements with us that provide our three television networks with a
substantial amount of programming. The Company currently pays a license fee of
approximately 15% of television net revenues to Televisa and Venevision for
their programming, subject to certain upward adjustments. The Company believes
that the program license agreements and all other agreements with Televisa and
Venevision have been negotiated as arms-length transactions.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Program License
Agreements</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our program license agreements (the &#147;Program License
Agreements&#148;) with each of Grupo Televisa S.A. and its affiliates (&#147;Televisa&#148;)
and affiliates of Corporacion Venezolana de Television, C.A. (VENEVISION) (&#147;Venevision&#148;)
extend until December&nbsp;2017. Under these agreements, we have the </font></p>

Venture</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2003, the
Company entered into a limited liability company agreement with Televisa Pay-TV
Venture,&nbsp;Inc. to form a 50/50 joint venture called TuTV LLC. The joint
venture was formed to broadcast Televisa&#146;s pay television channels, other than
general entertainment channels or novelas, in the United States. The service
consists of five channels. In May&nbsp;2003, TuTV entered into a five-year
distribution agreement with EchoStar Communications Corporation for three of
the channels. The joint venture is jointly controlled by Televisa and the
Company with each agreeing to fund up to a maximum of $20,000,000 over the
first three years of the venture. During 2005, the Company received a dividend of
$1,500,000 from TuTv LLC. In 2004, the Company and Televisa each funded the
joint venture $1,000,000.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">20</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3. Related Party Transactions (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Co-production
Agreement</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2003, the
Company and Televisa entered into an agreement whereby Televisa would produce
the show &#147;100 Mexicanos Dijeron&#148;, which is based on the &#147;Family Fued&#148; format
and the Company would pay Televisa approximately half of the costs per episode.
Under the terms of the agreement, the Company made payments of $4,700,000 and
$5,020,000 in 2005 and 2004, respectively, to Televisa in connection with the
production of the show. The Agreement with Televisa was not renewed but
production will continue in the U.S.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Share Purchase
Agreement</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2001, the
Company entered into a share purchase agreement with Televisa pursuant to which
Televisa purchased 375,000 preferred shares in exchange for $375,000,000. The
preferred shares automatically converted into 10,594,500 shares of the Company&#146;s
Class&nbsp;A Common Stock upon expiration of the waiting period under the
Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, on February&nbsp;25,
2002.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fonovisa Music
Group</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2002, we consummated the acquisition of
Fonovisa from Televisa for 6,000,000 shares of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock
and a warrant to purchase 100,000 shares of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock
(having an exercise price of $38.261 per share). Fonovisa has become a part of
our Univision Music Group. The purchase agreement for the acquisition included
certain working capital adjustments. In August&nbsp;2004, the Company and
Televisa finalized working capital adjustments related to the Company&#146;s
acquisition of Fonovisa, which was completed in April&nbsp;2002. The Company
received approximately $16,500,000, which has been accounted for as an
adjustment to the Fonovisa purchase price resulting in a reduction to goodwill
and minor adjustments to certain current assets and liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with our
acquisition of Fonovisa, we have the right to receive $5,000,000 of preemptable
advertising from Televisa in Mexico during each of the first three years after
the April&nbsp;2002 closing of such acquisition for the promotion of our music
business and its affiliates.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Univision Music
Group</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Univision Music Group consists of the businesses under
its wholly-owned subsidiary, Univision Music,&nbsp;Inc. The primary business
under Univision Music,&nbsp;Inc. is Univision Music LLC, which owns and
operates the Univision Records label, Fonovisa Records label, SGZ Records label
and La Calle label and whose membership units are owned 90% by the Company and
10% by Diara,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Diara&#148;), which is wholly-owned by Jos&#233; Behar,
President and Chief Executive Officer of Univision Music Group. Diara&#146;s
membership units consist solely of B-1 and B-2 units discussed
below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company amended its employment arrangement with
Jos&#233; Behar and assigned the employment agreement to Univision Music LLC, and as
a result, has amended the operating agreement of Univision Music LLC. Univision
Music LLC will now hold all of the Company&#146;s wholly-owned record labels. Also,
Diara has been given a new class of securities, designated &#147;B-2 Units&#148;
(and its existing units have been designated &#147;B-1 Units&#148;). In 2006, Diara
has a put right and the Company has a call right that would </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">21</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-21',FILE='C:\JMS\tosborn\06-1169-1\task924304\1169-1-fq.htm',USER='tosborna',CD='Mar 15 07:09 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3. Related Party Transactions (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">require the Company to
purchase all of Diara&#146;s B-1 Units for a purchase price equal to 20% of
ten times the average earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and
amortization of Univision Music&#146;s business as it existed prior to the
amendment, subject to a cap of $8,000,000. Additionally, Diara has a put right
and the Company has a call right on Diara&#146;s B-2 Units in 2009. To the
extent the fair market value of Univision Music LLC at the put or call date
exceeds the fair value at the grant date, which is decreased each year by the
amount of cash generated by Univision Music LLC, in December&nbsp;2003, the
purchase price of these units will be equal to 20% of the first $100,000,000 of
such excess, 10% of the next $100,000,000 of such excess and 1% of any excess
amount thereafter. This amount will be reduced by any amount paid by the
Company for the B-1 Units. The put and call rights may be accelerated in
the event of Mr.&nbsp;Behar&#146;s termination, death or disability.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is accounting for these arrangements in
accordance with FIN No.&nbsp;28 &#147;Accounting for Stock Appreciation Rights and
Other Variable Stock Option or Award Plans.&#148; FIN No.&nbsp;28 requires
compensation cost to be recognized when the quoted market value exceeds the
grant price. Compensation is charged to expense over the period the employee
performs the services. In 2005, 2004 and 2003, the Company recorded
approximately $1,600,0000, $4,300,000 and $1,700,000, respectively, of
compensation expense on the B-1 Units. In 2005, the Company recorded
approximately $4,200,000 of compensation expense on the B-2 units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The amended employment agreement with Mr.&nbsp;Behar
was extended through March&nbsp;31, 2009 and allows for minimum incentive bonus
amounts during each year&nbsp;and the payment in 2003 of
a&nbsp;$1,100,000&nbsp;bonus, which was&nbsp;applied against his outstanding
loan. The Company expensed this&nbsp;payment in 2003. As of December&nbsp;31,
2005, he owes approximately $900,000 in principal to the Company, which bears
interest at 3.5%.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">4.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Property

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">5. Intangible Assets and Goodwill</font>
(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has various intangible assets that are
being amortized.&#160; The Nielsen contract is
being amortized through December 2012, the Fonovisa contracts are being
amortized through June 2012, the Disa contracts are being amortized through
December 2011, the broadcast agreement is being amortized through January 2015,
advertiser related intangibles are being amortized through June 2006 and other
amortizable intangibles have various amortization periods.&#160; The Nielsen contract, broadcast agreement,
advertiser related intangibles, and a majority of the other amortizable intangibles
are being amortized on a straight-line basis.&#160;
The Fonovisa and Disa contracts are being amortized based on a revenue
allocation of the artist and songwriter contracts.&#160; The Company incurred amortization expense of
$14,128,000, $19,225,000 and $12,564,000 in 2005, 2004 and 2003 respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The changes in goodwill
are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cost Reduction Plan</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;2, 2005,
the Company announced a cost reduction plan that reduced its workforce and
abandoned certain less profitable programming in an effort to achieve
sustainable improvement in financial performance. The plan included reducing
approximately 5.6% of the workforce by eliminating job redundancies and
inefficiencies. The Company incurred a before-tax charge of approximately $30.3
million in the fourth quarter of 2005. The plan was substantially completed
during the fourth quarter of 2005 and the unpaid portion will primarily be paid
in 2006. The unpaid portion of the cost reduction plan as of December&nbsp;31,
2005 is as follows:</font></p>

<div align="center">

<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;">
 <tr>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost reduction charge
of $30,289,000 related to each of the Company&#146;s segments was $29,993,000,
$73,000, $33,000 and $190,000 for the television, radio, music and Internet
segments, respectively. At January&nbsp;31, 2006, the liability related to the
cost reduction plan was approximately $6,500,000.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s 7.85% senior notes due in 2011 have a
face value of $500,000,000 and bear simple interest at 7.85%. These senior
notes pay interest on January&nbsp;15 and July&nbsp;15 of each year. The notes
have a fair value of approximately $556,900,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;15, 2003, the Company issued three-,
four- and five-year senior notes due in 2006, 2007 and 2008 with a face value
of $700,000,000. These senior notes have a face value of $250,000,000,
$200,000,000 and $250,000,000, respectively. These senior notes pay simple
interest on April&nbsp;15 and October&nbsp;15 of each year. As part of the $700,000,000
note transaction the Company entered into a fixed-to-floating
interest rate swap that results in a fair value hedge that is perfectly
effective. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company had a swap liability with a
fair value of $13,977,000 reported in other long-term liabilities related to
this transaction. The $700,000,000 senior notes are carried at fair value at December&nbsp;31,
2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s senior notes are unsecured obligations,
equal in right of payment with all of the Company&#146;s existing and future senior
unsecured indebtedness, senior in right of payment to any of the Company&#146;s
future subordinated indebtedness and are fully and unconditionally guaranteed
by all of the Company&#146;s guarantors. The Company has the option to redeem all or
a portion of the senior notes at any time at the redemption prices set forth in
the note indenture. The indenture does not contain any provisions that would
require us to repurchase or redeem or otherwise modify the terms of the senior
notes upon a change of control. The indenture does not limit our ability to
incur indebtedness or require the maintenance of financial ratios or specified
levels of net worth or liquidity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company had a
$500,000,000 revolving credit facility with a syndicate of commercial lenders
that will mature on July&nbsp;18, 2006. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company
had bank borrowings outstanding under its revolving credit facility of
$314,000,000 resulting primarily from the Company&#146;s repurchases of its Class&nbsp;A
Common Stock. The Company classifies its revolving credit facility as a current
liability. The Company is in the process of negotiating a new bank credit
facility and expects to enter into a new credit agreement in the first quarter
of 2006. The Company has approximately $56,000,000 of letters of credit
outstanding under the credit facility, which primarily includes $49,000,000
related to the FIFA World Cup Agreement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans made under
the revolving credit facility bear interest determined by reference to LIBOR or
a base rate equal to the higher of the prime rate of Chase Manhattan Bank or
0.50% per annum over the </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:18.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">26</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-26',FILE='C:\fc\6713627226_D11448_887508\1169-1-fs.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar  8 01:37 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">7. Debt</font>
(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">federal funds rate.
Depending on the rating assigned by rating agencies to our senior unsecured debt,
the LIBOR interest rate margin on the Company&#146;s revolving credit facility
ranges from 0.75% to 1.5% per annum and the base rate margin ranges from 0% to
0.50% per annum. The Company&#146;s LIBOR interest rate margin applicable to the
revolving credit facility was 1.00% as of December&nbsp;31, 2005. The Company
borrows at the prime rate from time to time but attempts to maintain these
loans at a minimum. Interest is generally payable quarterly. During the twelve
months ended December&nbsp;2005, the Company&#146;s effective interest rate,
excluding deferred financing costs, on its bank debt and senior notes was
approximately 5.44%.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The credit agreement contains customary covenants,
including restrictions on liens and dividends and financial covenants relating
to interest coverage and maximum leverage. Under the credit agreement, the
Company is also limited in the amount of other debt it can incur and in its
ability to engage in mergers, sell assets and make material changes to its
Program License Agreements in a manner the lenders determine is materially
adverse to the Company. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company was in
compliance with its financial covenants.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The subsidiaries that guarantee the Company&#146;s
obligations under its credit agreement also guarantee the senior notes. The
subsidiary guarantors under the credit facilities are all of our domestic
subsidiaries other than certain immaterial subsidiaries. The guarantees are
full and unconditional and joint and several and any subsidiaries of the
Company other than the subsidiary guarantors are minor. Univision
Communications Inc. is not a guarantor and has no independent assets or
operations. The Company&#146;s variable interest entity, Disa, which is not
wholly-owned by the Company, does not guarantee the Company&#146;s bank credit agreement
or senior notes. The guarantees of the obligations under the revolving credit
facility and the senior notes will be released if our senior unsecured debt is
rated BBB or better by Standard&nbsp;&amp; Poor&#146;s Rating Services and Baa2 or
better by Moody&#146;s Investor Service,&nbsp;Inc. The guarantees of such subsidiary
will be reinstated if such ratings fall below BBB- by Standard&nbsp;&amp;
Poor&#146;s or Baa3 by Moody&#146;s. The Company&#146;s senior unsecured debt is currently
rated BBB- by Standard&nbsp;&amp; Poor&#146;s Rating Services and Baa2 by Moody&#146;s
Investor Service,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maturities of long-term
debt for the five years subsequent to December&nbsp;31, 2005 are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Commitments</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has long-term
operating leases expiring on various dates for office, studio, automobile and
tower rentals. The Company&#146;s operating leases, which are primarily related to
buildings and tower properties, have various renewal terms and escalation
clauses. The Company also has long-term capital lease obligations for its
transponders that are used to transmit and receive our network signals. In
2004, the </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;23, 2003, the Company entered into a
40-year lease for a three-story building with approximately 92,500 square
feet for the relocation of its owned and/or operated television and radio
stations and studio facilities in Puerto Rico. The building is to be
constructed and owned by the landlord, with occupancy of the premises expected
during the latter part of 2007. The lease was amended in June&nbsp;2005 and,
among other things, the term of the lease was extended from 40 to 50 years. The
sum of the lease payments will be approximately $74,000,000 over 50 years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2003, the Company entered into a transponder lease
agreement for TeleFutura Network that was capitalized in May&nbsp;2004 for
approximately $15,538,000. Also, in 2003, the Company entered into a transponder
lease agreement for Univision Network that is expected to be capitalized in the
first quarter 2006 for approximately $15,546,000. According to the Emerging
Issues Task Force published Issue 01-8 &#147;Determining Whether an
Arrangement Contains a Lease,&#148; if the Company negotiates a new transponder
lease agreement, the Company will not capitalize, or incur depreciation
expense, for its transponder lease agreements and will expense the cost as a
service fee. EITF 01-8 became effective for agreements entered into after
May&nbsp;2003. The Company does not expect to negotiate new transponder lease
agreements until two existing transponder lease agreements expire in
December&nbsp;2012. When and if the Company decides to transmit a high
definition signal, it will be required to negotiate new transponder leases.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2005, the Company entered into a new
seven-year contract with Nielsen Media Research (&#147;Nielsen&#148;), to provide local
market television programming ratings services for the Univision Television
Group and the TeleFutura Television Group at a total cost of approximately
$132,000,000. The aggregate payment remaining under the agreement, at
December&nbsp;31, 2005, is approximately $120,000,000, which will be paid
through February&nbsp;2012.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Commitments

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2002, the

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2001,

Caracas Television) to acquire approximately 780 hours of new novelas per year
through January&nbsp;2011. In 2005, the aggregate payment under the contract
was adjusted to approximately $72,181,000, with an aggregate payment remaining
under the contract of approximately $42,476,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2001,

approximately 300 hours of new novelas per year through June&nbsp;2007. The
aggregate payment under the contract is approximately $28,950,000 payable over
four years, in increasing installments, with an aggregate payment remaining
under the contract of approximately $1,650,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2002, 2003 and 2004,
the Company entered into several program license agreements to acquire approximately
2,000 movies. The agreements commenced in January&nbsp;2002 and expire on
various dates through March&nbsp;2016. The remaining payments under the
agreements are approximately $14,300,000, $10,400,000, $7,000,000, $4,100,000
and $674,000 for the years 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009 and the period January&nbsp;2010
through March&nbsp;2016, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of the
acquisition of the USA Broadcasting stations, the Company acquired
English-language programming contracts. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the
remaining payments are $2,560,000 in 2006, $1,662,000 in 2007, $1,395,000 in
2008, $1,351,000 in 2009 and $223,000 through February&nbsp;2010. The Company
is attempting to sub-license or arrange a sale of this programming to reduce
its liability.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2001, the
Company launched a music publishing and recording division, Univision Music
Group. In June&nbsp;2001, Univision Music Group acquired a 50% interest in Disa
Records from the Chavez family. The Company has a call right and the Chavez
family has a put right starting in June&nbsp;2006 that will require the Company
to purchase the remaining 50% interest for $75,000,000, subject to certain
upward adjustments. The Company expects that in 2006 it will exercise its
option to acquire the remaining 50% of Disa.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has various
music license agreements for its television and radio businesses. These
contracts grant the Company a license to broadcast musical compositions. The
remaining payments under these contracts are approximately $15,669,000,
$11,098,000, $7,848,000 and $4,648,000 in 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;2, 2005, the Company acquired the
Spanish-language broadcast rights in the U.S. to the 2010 and 2014 F&#233;d&#233;ration
Internationale de Football Association (&#147;FIFA&#148;) World Cup soccer games and
other&nbsp;2007 through 2014 FIFA events. A series of payments totaling
$325,000,000 is due over the term of the agreement, with approximately
$317,000,000 remaining as of December&nbsp;31, 2005. In addition to these
payments, and consistent with past coverage of the World Cup games, the Company
will be responsible for all costs associated with advertising, promotion and
broadcast of the World Cup games, as well as the production of certain
television programming related to the World Cup games.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8. Commitments (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;9,
2000, the Company acquired the Spanish-language broadcast rights in the U.S. to
the 2002 and 2006 FIFA World Cup soccer games and other 2000-2006 FIFA
events. The payments remaining at December&nbsp;31, 2005 totaled $66,000,000,
which is due in 2006. In addition to these payments, and consistent with past
coverage of the World Cup games, the Company was responsible for all costs
associated with advertising, promotion and broadcast of the World Cup games, as
well as the production of certain television programming related to the World
Cup games. The cost for the 2002 World Cup games was approximately $55,000,000.
</font>The rights fees are being amortized over the 2002/2006 World Cups and
other interim FIFA events based on the flow of income method. Under the flow of
income method, the costs for the 2006 World Cup games, excluding advertising,
promotion and broadcast costs, will be approximately $100,000,000 for the
rights fees. The funds for these payments
are expected to come from income from operations and/or borrowings from the
Company&#146;s revolving credit facility. In addition, the Company has also acquired
the Spanish-language broadcast rights in the U.S. for various sports contracts
with various expiration dates through November&nbsp;2007. The aggregate
payments under the contracts are approximately $78,900,000 at December&nbsp;31,
2005, the remaining payments under the contracts are approximately $8,400,000
in 2006 and $10,400,000 in 2007.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Employee
Benefits</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a 401(k)&nbsp;retirement
savings plan (the &#147;401(k)&nbsp;Plan&#148;) covering all eligible employees who have
completed one year of service. The 401(k)&nbsp;Plan allows the employees to
defer a portion of their annual compensation and the Company may match a
portion of the employees&#146; contributions. For the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, 2004 and 2003, the Company made matching cash contributions to the 401(k)&nbsp;Plan
totaling $6,194,000, $6,033,000 and $3,931,000, respectively. The Company
matches 100% of the first 3% of eligible employee compensation that was
contributed to the plan.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10. Contingencies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Televisa, S.A. de C.V. (&#147;Televisa&#148;) and the Company
are parties to a program license agreement (&#147;PLA&#148;) that provides our three
television networks with a majority of its prime time programming and a
substantial portion of its overall programming. The Company currently pays a
license fee to Televisa for programming, subject to certain upward adjustments.
On June&nbsp;16, 2005, Televisa&nbsp;filed an amended complaint in the United
States District Court for the Central District of California alleging breach by
us of our PLA with Televisa, including breach for our alleged failure to pay
Televisa royalties attributable to revenues from one of Univision&#146;s programs,
the Company&#146;s alleged unauthorized editing of certain Televisa programs and
related copyright infringement claims, a claimed breach of&nbsp;a&nbsp;soccer
rights&nbsp;side-letter to the PLA,&nbsp;and a claim that we have not been
properly carrying out a provision of the PLA that gives Televisa the secondary
right to use our unsold advertising&nbsp;inventory. Televisa seeks monetary
relief in an amount not less than $1.5 million for breach, anticipated breach,
declaratory relief against the Company&#146;s ability to recover amounts of
approximately $5.0 million previously paid in royalties to Televisa, and an
injunction against our alteration of Televisa programming without Televisa&#146;s
consent. On August&nbsp;15, 2005, the Company filed an answer to the amended
complaint denying Televisa&#146;s claims and also filed counterclaims alleging
various breaches of contract and covenants by Televisa. The Company seeks
monetary damages and injunctive relief.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">30</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-30',FILE='C:\fc\7395653125_D11492_917699\1169-1-fu.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 09:57 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">10. Contingencies</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;20,
2005, Televisa filed a motion to dismiss certain of the Company&#146;s counterclaims.
On November&nbsp;17, 2005, the District Court denied that motion in its
entirety. Thereafter, Televisa changed counsel and on January&nbsp;31, 2006&#151;after
several extensions of time granted by the Company&#151;Televisa filed its answer to
the Company&#146;s counterclaims. Without asserting any new matters of substance,
Televisa in its answer now alleges that its claims rise to the level of a
material breach of the PLA and delivered a purported notice of material breach
on February&nbsp;16, 2006. On March&nbsp;2, 2006, we responded to Televisa&#146;s
purported notice of material breaches. In our response, we asserted that the
notice was procedurally defective and that Televisa&#146;s breach claims were not,
in any event, well-founded. We do not believe that we are in breach of our
agreements with Televisa and certainly not in material breach. Univision
intends to take all action necessary to ensure Televisa&#146;s continued performance
under the PLA until its expiration in 2017. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the
Company accrued a charge of approximately $6&nbsp;million related to a payment the
Company intends to make under protest related to the Televisa litigation. The
Company will seek recovery of this amount via a counterclaim. We intend to
defend the litigation and pursue our counterclaims vigorously.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There are various other
legal actions and claims pending against the Company incidental to its business
and operations. In the opinion of management, the resolution of these matters
will not have a material effect on the consolidated financial position or
results of operations or liquidity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Approximately 33% of all
U.S. Hispanics live in the Los Angeles, New York and Miami-Fort Lauderdale
markets and the top ten U.S. Hispanic markets collectively account for
approximately 56% of the U.S. Hispanic population. Our revenues are similarly
concentrated in these key markets. As a result, an economic downturn, increased
competition, or another significant negative event in these markets could
reduce our revenues and results of operations more dramatically than other
companies that do not depend as much on these markets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains
insurance coverage for various risks, where deemed appropriate by management,
at rates and terms that management considers reasonable. The Company
self-insures its employee medical benefits and its media errors and omissions
exposures. The Company also has deductibles for various risks, including those
associated with windstorm and earthquake damage. In management&#146;s opinion, the
potential exposure in future periods, if uninsured losses were to be incurred,
should not be material to the consolidated financial position or results of
operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11. Income

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">11. Income
Taxes</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for
income taxes under the liability method pursuant to SFAS No.&nbsp;109 &#147;Accounting
for Income Taxes.&#148; Deferred income taxes reflect the net tax effects of
temporary differences between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities
for financial reporting purposes and the amounts used for income tax purposes.
Significant components of the Company&#146;s deferred tax assets and liabilities as
of December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004 are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recorded a
deferred tax asset of $32,014,000 relating to the nontemporary decline in the
value of its investments in Entravision and the St. Louis/Denver joint venture,
offset by a valuation allowance for the same amount since, based on the weight
of available evidence, it is more likely than not the deferred tax asset
recorded will not be realized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of various acquisitions, the Company
recorded goodwill representing the consideration given in excess of the fair
value of net assets acquired. No deferred tax liability is established for
goodwill that is not deductible for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12. Earnings Per Share</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company is required to calculate basic earnings per share, which is computed by
dividing income available to common stockholders (the numerator) by the
weighted-average number of common shares outstanding (the denominator) during
the period. The Company is also required to compute diluted earnings per share,
which is similar to basic earnings per share, except that the denominator is
increased to include the number of additional common shares that would have
been outstanding if the dilutive potential common shares had been issued. The
following is the reconciliation of the numerator and the denominator of the
basic and diluted earnings-per-share computations:</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13. Common Stock,
Preferred Stock and Warrants</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s common stock consists of Class&nbsp;A,
Class&nbsp;P, Class&nbsp;T and Class&nbsp;V shares. The Class&nbsp;A shares are
listed on the New York Stock Exchange and are primarily held by non-affiliates.
The Class&nbsp;P, T&nbsp;and V shares are held by affiliates and are not
traded. All classes of common stock have substantially the same rights, with
the exception of Class&nbsp;P shares, which have ten votes per share on all
matters on which shareholders are entitled to vote and Class&nbsp;T and V,
which each have the right to elect one member of the Company&#146;s board of
directors. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, there were 236,589,943 shares of
Class&nbsp;A Common Stock issued and outstanding, 36,962,390 shares of
Class&nbsp;P Common Stock issued and outstanding, 13,593,034 shares of
Class&nbsp;T Common Stock issued and outstanding and 17,837,164 of Class&nbsp;V
Common Stock issued and outstanding. The Company&#146;s Class&nbsp;A Common Stock
outstanding decreased during 2005 by 18,349,317 shares from 254,939,260 to
236,589,943 due to a decrease of 19,096,600 resulting from the repurchase of
treasury shares and an increase of 747,283 due the exercise of options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;17, 2005, the Company announced that
its Board of Directors had approved the repurchase of up to $500 million of its
outstanding Class&nbsp;A Common Stock. On October&nbsp;24, 2005, the Company
completed repurchasing approximately $500 million, 19,096,600 shares, in
accordance with its stock repurchase plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;1, 2005, the Company&#146;s Board of
Directors approved the repurchase of an additional $500 million of its
outstanding Class&nbsp;A Common Stock. The share repurchases will be made in
the open market or negotiated transactions as market and business conditions
warrant, subject to securities laws and other legal requirements. The share
repurchase plan will expire on December&nbsp;31, 2006. No shares have been
repurchased pursuant to the plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;21, 2005, the Company retired the
20,113,780 shares that it held in treasury. This amount represents the
19,096,600 shares that were repurchased during 2005 and the 1,017,180 shares
held by the Company at December&nbsp;31, 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had 10,000,000 shares of preferred stock,
$.01 par value, authorized at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2005, Televisa and Venevision
owned a total of 9,102,000 and 30,237,700 warrants, respectively. These
warrants include 27,439,700 warrants issued in 1992 that are exercisable for
Class&nbsp;T and Class&nbsp;V Common Stock at an exercise price of $0.0322 per
share. The Company accounted for the warrants issued to Televisa and Venevision
within stockholders&#146; equity, except for the 100,000 warrants issued in
connection with the Fonovisa acquisition that have been accounted for as part
of its purchase price.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Televisa and Venevision warrants cannot be
exercised by either Televisa or Venevision (or by any other non-U.S.
citizen) if such exercise would result in a violation of the foreign ownership
restrictions of the Communications Act of 1934. Subject to certain
restrictions, Televisa and Venevision may transfer such warrants.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If Televisa and Venevision were to exercise their
warrants, their ultimate ownership of the Company would be approximately 12%
for Televisa and 15% for Venevision.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">34</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As part of the consent decree pursuant to which the
United States Department of Justice (&#147;DOJ&#148;) approved our acquisition of
Hispanic Broadcasting Corporation, the Company exchanged all of its Entravision
voting common stock for 36,926,600 shares of Class&nbsp;U common stock. The
Entravision Class&nbsp;U common stock has limited voting rights and does not
include the right to elect directors. Also, as part of the consent decree with
the DOJ, we are required to sell enough of our Entravision stock so that our
ownership of Entravision on a fully converted basis, which includes full
conversion of employee options and all convertible securities, does not exceed
15% by March&nbsp;26, 2006 and 10% by March&nbsp;26, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recorded a charge of $24,741,000 for the
three months ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, related to an other than temporary
decline in the value of its Entravision stock. The charge is based on the fair
value of our investment in Entravision common stock of $7.12 per share on the
last trading day of 2005 compared to our average cost basis of $7.79 per share.
The Company&#146;s new cost basis in its investment in Entravision stock is now
$7.12. Entravision&#146;s stock price at March&nbsp;9, 2006 was $7.60. Any gain or
loss on future transactions involving Entravision stock will be measured by
comparing our newly established cost basis of $7.12 per share to the fair value
of the Entravision stock at the transaction date. The Company recorded a charge
of $48,336,000 for the three months ended June&nbsp;30, 2005, related to an
other than temporary decline in the value of its Entravision stock. We will
continue to monitor the Entravision stock price, its operating results, the
performance and outlook for the media sector in general and other information
available to determine if the value of our investment becomes other than
temporarily impaired in subsequent reporting periods. The future sale of the
stock will have no impact on the Company&#146;s existing television station
affiliation agreements with Entravision. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company&#146;s
ownership of Entravision on a fully converted basis was approximately 27%. Following
the acquisition of </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;7, 2002, the Company, through its

respectively. The TeleFutura TBA became effective on February&nbsp;23, 2003. On
October&nbsp;1, 2005, the Company performed its annual impairment testing
analysis and obtained an appraised value of the Denver and St. Louis FCC
licenses, which are the primary assets of the LLC. Based in part on this
appraisal, the Company determined that the fair value of its investment in the
LLC was less than the book carrying value and recorded an impairment charge of
$8.8 million in the fourth quarter of 2005. In 2005, the Company also reported
an equity loss from unconsolidated subsidiary of $580,000 and the investment
had $143,000 of other increases related to the joint venture.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2001, the Company completed the
acquisition of a 50% interest in Disa Records for approximately $75,000,000 in
cash. In addition, the Company agreed to provide $5,000,000 per year of
advertising to Disa Records for the five-year period July&nbsp;1, 2001 to June&nbsp;30,
2006. On March&nbsp;31, 2004, the Company was required to adopt Financial
Accounting Standards Board Interpretation No.&nbsp;46, &#147;Consolidation of
Variable Interest Entities&#148;, (&#147;FIN 46&#148;). Under the guidelines of FIN 46, the
Company is required to consolidate the assets, liabilities and operating
results of Disa, which is owned 50% by the Company and 50% by the Chavez
family. The use of the equity method of accounting prior to March&nbsp;31, 2004
and the consolidation of Disa since April&nbsp;1, 2004 have the same effect on
the Company&#146;s net income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2001, the Company purchased for

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2004, the

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14. Investments

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">paid in
preference to all other junior stock as and when declared or on liquidation, is

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2003, the
Company entered into a limited liability company agreement with Televisa Pay-TV
Venture,&nbsp;Inc. to form a 50/50 joint venture called TuTV LLC. See note &#147;3.
Related Party Transactions.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Variable Interest
Entities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;31, 2004,
the Company was required to adopt Financial Accounting Standards Board
Interpretation No.&nbsp;46, &#147;Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities&#148;, (&#147;FIN
46&#148;). FIN 46 expands upon and strengthens existing accounting guidance that
addresses when a company should consolidate in its financial statements the
assets, liabilities and operating results of another entity. Under previous
guidance, a company generally included another entity in its consolidated
financial statements only if it controlled the entity through voting interests.
FIN 46 requires a variable interest entity (&#147;VIE&#148;) to be consolidated by a
company if that company is the &#147;primary beneficiary&#148; of that entity. An entity
is a VIE if, among other things, it has equity investors that do not absorb the
expected losses or receive the expected returns of the entity. The primary
beneficiary is subject to a majority of the risk of loss from the VIE&#146;s
activities, or is entitled to receive a majority of the VIE&#146;s residual returns,
or both.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the guidelines of
FIN 46, since March&nbsp;31, 2004, the Company has been required to consolidate
the assets, liabilities and operating results of Disa Records, which is a
Mexico-based music recording and publishing company, owned 50% by the Company
and 50% by the Chavez family, who manages the business. The Company has a call
right and the Chavez family has a put right, beginning in June&nbsp;2006, which
requires the Company to purchase the remaining 50% of Disa Records for a
minimum of $75,000,000, subject to certain upward adjustments. The Company
expects that in 2006 it will exercise its option to acquire the remaining 50%
of Disa. As a result of Disa&#146;s put right, the Company has the majority of
expected losses that could arise from the variability of the fair value of Disa
Records. Under the rules&nbsp;governing FIN 46, the Company is&nbsp;considered
the primary beneficiary of Disa Records and consequently is required to
consolidate it.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, under the
guidelines of FIN 46, since March&nbsp;31, 2004, the Company was required to
consolidate the assets, liabilities, and operating results of the Puerto Rico
stations, WLII/WSUR,&nbsp;Inc., a Delaware corporation (&#147;WLII&#148;), which were
wholly-owned by Raycom Media,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Raycom&#148;). On June&nbsp;30, 2005, the
Company acquired Raycom&#146;s ownership interest in WLII in Puerto Rico for
approximately $190,000,000, excluding acquisition costs. The funds came
primarily from the Company&#146;s bank credit facility. WLII is now a wholly owned
subsidiary of the Company and is no longer a VIE.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior periods were not
restated upon the adoption of FIN 46. Since the Company adopted FIN 46 on March&nbsp;31,
2004, the operating results of Disa Records and WLII are not included in the
operating results of the Company for the three months ended March&nbsp;31,
2004. Beginning April&nbsp;1, 2004, Disa Records&#146; net revenues and operating
income were included in the Company&#146;s operating results and the Company&#146;s net </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">37</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14. Investments
and Variable Interest Entities (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">income
remained the same, as it would have been under the equity method of accounting
that we used before we adopted FIN 46. WLII&#146;s net revenues and operating income
were also included in the Company&#146;s operating results from April&nbsp;1, 2004
through June&nbsp;30, 2005, but our net income was not affected since Raycom
owned 100% of WLII in 2004 and for the six months ended June&nbsp;30, 2005. The
Company will continue to consolidate Disa Records under the guidelines of FIN
46 until the Company exercises its call right or the Chavez family exercises
their put right and the Company purchases Disa Records. The Company has
consolidated the results of operations of WLII under the guidelines of FIN 46
for the six months ended June&nbsp;30, 2005 and continues to consolidate WLII
from June&nbsp;30, 2005 forward since WLII is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of
the Company.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15. Performance Award and
Incentive Plans</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a 1996 and 2004 Performance Award Plan
(the &#147;Plans&#148;). The 2004 Performance Award Plan (&#147;2004 Plan&#148;) reserves shares of
Class&nbsp;A Common Stock for issuance to Company officers, key employees and
other eligible persons as determined by the Board of Directors or Plan
Committee (as appointed by the Board). The Company no longer issues new awards
under its 1996 Performance Award Plan (&#147;1996 Plan&#148;) but the plan continues to
have grants outstanding.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2004 Plan was adopted as of May&nbsp;2004, in
part, to increase the maximum number of shares of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock
currently available under the 1996 Plan and to give the Company sufficient
authority and flexibility to adequately provide for future incentives. A total
of 15,936,550 shares of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock were registered under the
2004 Plan, 12,600,000 shares were made available under the 2004 Plan and
3,336,550 shares were made available from the 1996 Plan. The maximum number of
shares that may be granted to any individual during any calendar year is
3,000,000. The maximum number of shares that may be granted during any calendar
year is 5,000,000 (not including those shares, if any, that have been cancelled
during the same year they were granted) unless the Plan Committee gives its
unanimous consent. The Plan provides that shares granted come from the
Company&#146;s authorized but unissued Class&nbsp;A Common Stock and any shares of
the Company&#146;s Class&nbsp;A Common Stock held as treasury shares. Grants may be
in the form of either nonqualified stock options, incentive stock options,
stock appreciation rights, restricted stock awards, restricted stock unit
awards, performance share awards, stock bonuses or cash bonus awards.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">40</font></p>

<div>
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15. Performance
Award and Incentive Plans (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The price of the options
granted pursuant to the Plans may not be less than 100% of the fair market
value of the shares on the date of grant (110% in the case of an incentive
stock option granted to any person owning more than 10% of the Company&#146;s total
combined voting power). No award will be exercisable after ten years from the
date granted. Unless approved by the Plan Committee, no award may vest at a
rate greater than 25% per year, other than in the case of awards granted in
lieu of cash bonuses, which may vest at the rate of 50% per year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;14,
2005, the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company
approved the acceleration of vesting of substantially all unvested stock options
outstanding whose exercise price was above the then current market price of
$25.56. The Compensation Committee&#146;s decision to accelerate the vesting of the
affected stock options was based upon the issuance by the Financial Accounting
Standards Board of Statement of Financial Accounting Standard No.&nbsp;123
(Revised 2004), &#147;Share-Based Payment&#148; which requires the Company to treat
unvested stock options as compensation expense effective January&nbsp;1, 2006. Because
the Company accounts for stock based compensation using the intrinsic value
method prescribed in Accounting Principles Board (APB) No.&nbsp;25, and because
these options were priced above current market on that date, the acceleration
of vesting of these options did not result in a charge in the Company&#146;s
financial statements. Vesting acceleration increased pro forma stock based
compensation, under the provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;123 by approximately $59
million before income tax. Assuming that there are no modifications to the
affected options, the Company believes that it will not be required to
recognize any compensation expense in future periods associated with the
affected options. As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, substantially all of the
Company&#146;s outstanding options have been expensed due to the acceleration.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the acquisition of HBC on September&nbsp;22,
2003, the Company assumed outstanding stock options previously issued under the
HBC Long-Term Incentive Plan. The assumed stock option and their respective
grant price have been converted in accordance with the acquisition agreement.
No new awards were granted under this plan upon and following the acquisition.
The maximum term of each assumed option is ten years from the original grant
date, subject to earlier termination in connection with the recipient&#146;s
termination of employment with or service to the Company. The assumed options
vest in accordance with the HBC Long-Term Incentive Plan and the acquisition
agreement.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15. Performance
Award and Incentive Plans (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, 759,183 options were exercised from the Company&#146;s option plans for
759,183 shares of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock, resulting in increases to common
stock and paid-in-capital of approximately $7,000 and $14,854,000,
respectively, which included a tax benefit of $4,236,000 associated with the
transactions.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16. Business Segments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s principal business segment is television, which includes the
operations of the Company&#146;s Univision Network, TeleFutura Network, Galavisi&#243;n
and owned-and-operated stations and the variable interest entity, WLII. In September&nbsp;2003,
the Company completed its acquisition of HBC, now called Univision Radio. The
operating segments reported below are the segments of the Company for which
separate financial information is available and for which segment results are
evaluated regularly by management in deciding how to allocate resources and in
assessing performance. Presented below is segment information pertaining to the
Company&#146;s television, radio, music and Internet businesses.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">UNIVISION COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)<br> December 31, 2005</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16. Business
Segments (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses
the key indicator of &#147;operating income before depreciation and amortization&#148;
primarily to evaluate the Company&#146;s operating performance and for planning and
forecasting future business operations. In addition, this key indicator is
commonly used as a measure of performance for broadcast companies, is used by
investors to measure a company&#146;s ability to service debt and other cash needs
and provides investors the opportunity to evaluate the Company&#146;s performance as
it is viewed by management. Operating income before depreciation and
amortization is not, and should not be used as, an indicator of or an
alternative to operating income, net income or cash flow as reflected in the
consolidated financial statements, is not a measure of financial performance
under generally accepted accounting principles (&#147;GAAP&#148;) and should not be
considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures of performance prepared
in accordance with GAAP. Since the definition of operating income before
depreciation and amortization may vary among companies and industries it should
not be used as a measure of performance among companies. In accordance with SEC
guidelines, the Company is providing on a consolidated basis a reconciliation
of the non-GAAP term operating income before depreciation and amortization to
net income, which is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, for
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003:</font></p>
